values: Materials and setup｜all a fictional dormitory tabletop drill

You are the duty advisor for a school dormitory. The following A1—A5 are fictional materials, used only to practice incident grading, records, notification, and handover; they do not represent any school's protocols or real resident information.

A1｜Tuesday 18:00 duty log: the door lock in Room 302 of Building B has an intermittent fault, the maintenance work order was submitted but has no receipt; the second-floor shared kitchen trash has not been cleared; a resident social event is at 19:30.

A2｜18:20 Resident A reports that the Room 302 door lock cannot close properly and the room is empty; Resident B says they saw a stranger try the door last night. The time and identity have not been verified.

A3｜18:35 Two residents argue about nighttime noise, with no physical conflict on site; one of them says “I can't take it anymore”, but the meaning is unclear. Safety and immediate risk must be checked first, with no diagnosis on one's own.

A4｜18:45 The maintenance team replies that the Room 302 door lock will be inspected before 20:00; if it cannot be repaired, alternative accommodation arrangements must be approved by the duty supervisor. Another staff member can continue organizing the activity.

A5｜fictional duty rules: advisors may verify facts, temporarily isolate danger, contact the duty supervisor and the maintenance team, and keep records; for urgent safety risks, contact emergency personnel immediately per organizational protocols; they must not disclose resident identities, diagnose independently, or promise accommodations beyond their authority.
Task and outputs

Using A1—A5, write a one-page incident grading table: list the known, unknown, and safety facts requiring immediate verification, and arrange the next steps for the door lock, the dispute, sanitation, and the activity separately.

Then write a minimum necessary handover record containing the time, person acting, notification recipients, receipts, and closure conditions; fictional resident names or unverified allegations must not be treated as facts.
Reference approach (complete it independently first)

First verify on site whether the Room 302 door lock cannot close and whether there is personal or property risk; the stranger report is not yet substantiated, so explain it to the supervisor per protocol and arrange temporary safety measures. Track the maintenance receipt before 20:00, and if it is not repaired the duty supervisor decides on alternative accommodation; hand the shared kitchen sanitation to the owner, and another staff member can continue organizing the 19:30 activity.

For the dispute, first confirm both parties' safety, check their accounts separately, and clarify whether “I can't take it anymore” indicates immediate risk such as self-harm; with danger signals, immediately use the organizational emergency chain and make no diagnosis. Hand the kitchen sanitation and the activity to clear owners; at handover keep the unfinished items, follow-up time, and next shift contact.

entries.answer: Residential advisors center on daily order, activities, records, and resident support in settings such as school dormitories and group homes; social and human service assistants focus more on case needs and social resource connection. description.text: Residential advisors support residents, coordinate activities, patrol, and hand over issues in residential facilities such as school dormitories and group homes. Learn about entry conditions, duty risks, US wage and employment data, and the Chinese pay evidence gap.

subject.name: Residential Advisors
subject.summary: Residential advisors coordinate activities, respond to resident issues, enforce rules, and keep handover records in residential facilities such as school dormitories or group homes; when health, safety, or professional issues arise, they refer promptly under the organization's protocols. Specific shifts and permissions depend on the position.
